# Projection on White Model — Style Prompt

> A pure white massing model of a real place stands on a plinth in a dark room, and a projector paints data onto it as light: one layer at a time, falling on the surfaces that face it, spilling a little past the plate. The model never changes; only the light on it does.
> References (grammar only): projection-mapped planning models in city galleries (the dark room, the soft throw, colour only on white surfaces); macro model photography (shallow focus at rooftop height); editorial data graphics (one figure, one label, one source per layer). Copy none of their layouts, typefaces, colours or music, and never name them in the film.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

- **The model is real geometry of a real place**: building footprints and heights from open data (§2), extruded at a stated scale (1:1000, 1:2000…). Nothing on the model is invented or "representative", and no generated image ever stands in for the place.
- **The model is white; data is light.** Colour is never painted into the material: it is projected, so it brightens surfaces that face the projector, fades on walls turned away, stops at the edge of the throw and reaches a little onto the plinth.
- **Layers arrive one at a time**, each with its own gesture of light (a wash, a pop-on, a rising level, a moving sun), and each answers the question the last one raised.
- **A physical room**: house lights, a projector that strikes and switches, a plinth, darkness around it. Lights out is where the data starts; lights up is where it ends.
- **Every number on screen is computed from the same buildings** that are on the table.

Not Isometric Infographic (no diorama or icons), not Low-poly Island (no invented terrain), not Sci-fi Hologram HUD (no wireframes; light lands on matter), not Satellite Briefing (no imagery), not a laser-scan or point-cloud film (no scan lines; light is projected, not measured).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Model**: matte white (≈ #F3F3F1, roughness ≈ 0.9), crisp edges; water a darker satin inlay in the base plate; bridges low white slabs; a thin base plate on a dark satin plinth.
- **Light model**: house light = one soft key + a neutral studio environment + AO on close shots. Projection = a term added to the lit surface in the shader: `colour × (0.42 + 0.58 · max(N·toProjector, 0)) × throw mask`, scaled by albedo, reduced on water. Never a texture on the mesh.
- **Building data is the material.** First look for the place's own open 3D or footprint-with-height data: 3DBAG (Netherlands, CC BY 4.0), PLATEAU (Japan, CC BY 4.0-compatible), city open-data portals (footprints with heights or floors, zoning, plans). Fine: CC0, public domain, CC BY (credited in CREDITS and on screen). OpenStreetMap and Overture (ODbL), CC BY-SA and "no known restrictions" are not CC0: name the terms to the user and ask first. For their own site, ask the user for their data (plan, city model, survey heights).
- **Layers depend on what exists.** Construction years per building are a Dutch luxury (BAG); elsewhere they are often missing. Substitute what the data does hold and the medium can still project: heights or floor counts, footprint area, zoning or plan status, a boundary, sun and shadow (always computable). Never invent a year layer.
- **A layer is state, not a picture**: per-building attributes (year, height, rank, flags) live in vertex data; the shader decides each frame what colour the projector gives them.
- **The sun is a real directional light** with shadow maps, computed from the place's latitude and a real date and time (NOAA/Meeus solar position). The projector can trace what the sun does (a shadow footprint) but never fakes a shadow.
- **Post**: physical depth of field (stronger on close shots), bloom only above the projection highlights, vignette, light grain in ffmpeg. GTAO only on close shots: on wide grazing views it bands.
- **Screen space only for the 2D layer**: readouts, pins, measured lines and subtitles go through the camera's world → screen function so they stay pinned to the model.
- **Keep a FACTS.md in the project folder** (claim, source URL, quoted wording, or the measurement method) and deliver it with the film; every number on screen is computed by a script from the same data as the model.

## 3. Colour logic

- Neutral ground: white model, dark room (near black), dark plinth. Projector black level is a cool near-black on the plate.
- **One hue family per layer**, chosen for the data: a single categorical accent for "the old/the exception" (e.g. warm amber), a sequential ramp for continuous data (blue → cyan → white for time, violet → magenta → peach for height).
- **A colour may return** only with the same meaning (the "before" colour reused later marks the same set of buildings).
- The sun is warm, its shade is a projected deep blue; data colours are put away when the sun arrives.
- Never colour the model in the house light; never use more than two layer palettes on screen at once.

## 4. Type & subtitles

- **Roles**: a light grotesk for the figure (Inter Tight 200, 120–140 px), a sans for labels in the film's language (Noto Sans SC 300/500, 20–36 px), a monospace for instruments, years and coordinates (IBM Plex Mono, 18–22 px). OFL, self-hosted, CJK subset.
- **Readout in the left third**, one per layer: index + layer name, one figure, one label, one source line, a legend bar.
- **Pins**: a hairline from a roof or a ground point up to a tag on a dark plate (title 26 px + one sub line 20 px).
- **Identity label** top-left, quiet: place, scale, data sources.
- **Subtitles** centred at the bottom on a soft dark gradient, no box, measured with the real fonts; if the film is bilingual, the film's language on top, each language on a single line, split into two cues rather than wrap.
- Nothing below 18 px at 1080p. Hold subtitles ≥ max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s); labels ≥ characters ÷ 4.5 + 1.5 s (CJK), letters ÷ 15 + 1.5 s (Latin).

## 5. Motion quality

- The camera moves continuously and slowly; it changes speed with the layers, never stops dead.
- **Light is the actor.** Each layer arrives by a soft-edged gesture of light: a wash spreading from the projector axis, buildings switching on one by one with a short flash, a level climbing every facade, the sun's clock running. No hard line sweeping the table.
- House lights cut fast (a relay, 0.25 s) and return slowly (1 s); the projector strikes with a brief flicker.
- Counters roll while the light moves and land when it lands; measured lines grow from A to B with ticks.
- What never moves: the model, the plinth, the pins' anchors on the model.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Macro glide at rooftop height, shallow focus | the model is a real object | an opening; a detail that matters |
| Crane up and back | the whole pattern only seen from above | revealing a hole, a cluster, an edge |
| Slow orbit with a rise | the city as a whole, layers accumulating | growth over time; comparisons across the model |
| Boom down to a low angle against black | height, skyline | tall buildings, heights, a single tower |
| Side-on track along a line | a measured distance on the model | a shadow, a corridor, a route, a view line |
| Pull back as the house lights return | the data stops; the object remains | an ending; a reset between topics |

At key moments the subject fills a third of the frame height; readouts left third, subtitles bottom centre, pins never over the readout. Transitions are light changes on one take (lights out, a layer replacing another, the projector going dark), not cuts, fades or wipes.

## 7. Sound palette

- **The room**: room tone, the projector fan (hum + filtered air) rising when the lamp strikes, relays for the house lights, a lamp strike (zap + thump), the air of a light wash (sliding band-passed noise).
- **Light as sound**: mallets and glass for things switching on, bowed vibraphone for held light, a rising mallet line and air riser for a climbing level, one glass note per highlighted building.
- **Weight**: timpani, gran cassa, gong, low brass for a heavy fact; warm low brass for a turn.
- **Floor**: contrabass and cellos only as a floor under the chords; no generic piano and strings melody.
- **Silence**: the projector goes dark and everything stops but a thin fan hum before the turn; a short suck-out before the heaviest hit. The first sound after the silence is the turn.
- **Mix**: voice about 10 dB over the music; the two designed impacts are the loudest moments; −14 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1.2 dB. Voice: calm, short declarative lines, numbers spoken plainly.

## 8. Native moves

- **Lights out, lamp on.** House light, a relay, darkness, the lamp strikes, the first layer arrives. *Fits content like:* a site before and after; a district before a plan is shown; any "now look closer".
- **The hole.** Light only the set that answers a question (built before a date, owned by one party, inside a zone) and let the absence draw the shape. *Fits content like:* a war-damaged centre; a flood plain with no housing; land a company owns; a protected zone.
- **Layers by time.** Buildings switch on in the decade they were built, each layer faster than the last, a year counter rolling. *Fits content like:* a new town's growth; a campus master plan by phase; a port's expansion; a developer's portfolio by year.
- **The rising level.** A soft level of light climbs every facade at once; low buildings finish first, the tallest last, the reading rides up with it. *Fits content like:* building heights; sea-level or flood depth; floor counts; a height limit being tested.
- **The sun clock.** A real sun at a real date sweeps the shadows; the projector then traces one shadow and measures it. *Fits content like:* a new tower's shadow on a park; winter light in a courtyard; solar panels' best roofs; a street's daylight hours.
- **The pick-out.** One building or set lights alone while the rest stay dark, with a pin. *Fits content like:* a listed building; the plot for sale; the hospital in an evacuation plan.
- **Lights up.** The data stops, the white model comes back. An ending or a reset.

## 9. Pitfalls of the medium

- **Wall normals** wound the wrong way show inside faces (walls look hollow): derive the outward normal from ring orientation. **Shared walls** between parts z-fight: skip the overlap below the lower neighbour.
- **Warm HDRIs turn the white model beige**: use a neutral studio environment.
- **GTAO on wide grazing views** produces wedge-shaped dark bands; keep it on close shots only.
- **A low sun lights facades, not roofs**: shoot from the sunlit side or side-on. **Narrow shadows vanish** among all the others: trace the one that matters (fill + edge) and measure it.
- **Hairline scan lines read as laser scanning**: give every projection front a wide soft edge or switch buildings individually.
- **Floating labels**: anchor pins on the tallest part of a building, not on its footprint centroid.
- **Numbers from mixed sources** (official height vs measured roof): say which on screen ("roof", "measured").

## 10. Engine

- `demo/studio.js` — `makeStudio(W, H, model)`: renderer, post, room, the projection material (`projMaterial(kind)` injects `projLight()` / `roofGlow()` into MeshStandardMaterial), the city mesh (`buildCity`: outward normals, shared walls removed), plate, plinth, house light (index 0) and sun (index 1). Uniforms `U` drive every layer.
- `demo/tools/prep.py` — **3DBAG + BGT only**: it reads 3DBAG fields (`b3_h_70p`, `b3_h_maaiveld`, `oorspronkelijkbouwjaar`) and Dutch RD coordinates (`tools/rd.py`). Another source needs its own adapter that writes the same `model.json`: `{size:[w,d] model metres, b:[[year|0, height_m], …] per building, p:[[building_index, height_model_m, [[[x,z],…] outer ring, …holes]], …] per roof part, decks:[[[x,z],…]]}`, with x east, z south, 1 unit = 1 model metre; plus `water.png` (plate-sized mask) and a `stats.json` with every on-screen number. `tools/sun.py` (solar position, any place and date) and the heightfield shadow are source-independent.
- `demo/overlay.js` — readout, pin, measured range line, subtitle strip, title card; registers texts for readcheck.
- **Extra packages and packs**: none beyond `setup.sh deps` (+ `voice`, `music` for narration and score); downloads are plain `curl` from the data portal. Reprojecting another country's data may need pyproj or shapely: the agent installs them itself into a private venv in the project folder, not into `$LIB/.venv`.
- Minimal example, not in the demo: set `U.uPreC` to a station and `U.uPreR` growing to light everything within walking distance; or put a flood height in `U.uHgtF` with `U.uHgtBand` held at 1 and leave it still.

## 11. Variation space

Decide per film: place and scale, which layers in what order, their colours, the opening, the camera path, the ending, the pace.

- **Structures**: a question answered layer by layer; a plan versus today (the plan's buildings switching on in a second colour); one building's story told by its neighbours.
- **Openings**: a macro glide over white roofs; darkness and a single pick-out; the plinth from across the room as the house lights fall.
- **Endings**: lights up on the white model; one last layer left on alone; the camera rising until the model is an object on a table in a dark room.

---

How our demo was made (story, shots, score, title card, build): [DEMO.md](DEMO.md). Read it after your treatment exists.

# Projection on White Model — our demo

One example among many. Don't reuse its story, arc, shots, props or timings.

Demo: *How a Flattened City Grew Back* 《被炸平的城市怎样长回来》 (40.0 s) · `white-model.mp4` · source in [`demo/`](demo/)

Rotterdam's centre as a 1:1000 white model (2.3 × 2.6 km: 3,887 buildings, 8,860 roof parts, 108 bridge decks). Chinese on screen, English narration, bilingual subtitles (Chinese line above, English line below).

## Story & structure

Logline: light picks out everything on the model built before 1940 and finds a hole in the middle; decade by decade the hole fills and the city climbs; then the tallest new tower's midwinter-noon shadow runs 777 m across sixteen roofs, nine of them pre-war.

Arc: the white model under gallery light → lights out, the lamp strikes, the pre-war layer (23 % of the footprint) and the hole → 14 May 1940, 13:27; the city hall that came through almost undamaged → four post-war layers pop on, faster each time, a year counter rolling 1940 → 2025; the city crosses the river (Kop van Zuid) → a level of light climbs every facade and tops out on Zalmhaven I (roof 203 m); 24 of the 25 buildings over 100 m are post-1990 → the projector goes dark (silence) → the winter sun at solar noon (14.6°), the tower's shadow traced and measured (777 m), the sixteen roofs inside it light up, the nine pre-war ones in the first layer's amber → house lights up, white model, end card.

Native moves spent: *lights out, lamp on* at 1.8–2.4 s; *the hole* for 1940; *layers by time* for the growth; *the rising level* for heights; *the sun clock* plus a projected shadow trace and a range line as the signature; *the pick-out* for the roofs; *lights up* as the bookend.

Every number on screen is computed by `demo/tools/prep.py` into `demo/data/stats.json`; every claim and its source is in [`demo/FACTS.md`](demo/FACTS.md).

## Shots

One continuous take. Camera = target, azimuth (0 = south of the target looking north, 90 = east), elevation, distance in model metres.

| # | Time | Shot | Camera | Native move / note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.0–1.8 | white roofs at rooftop height, shallow focus, gallery light, AO | macro glide from the north-east (az 152 → 142, el 7 → 11, d 0.55 → 0.72) | the model as an object |
| 2 | 1.8–2.4 | house lights cut (0.25 s), darkness | glide continues | relay; silence of the room |
| 3 | 2.4–6.0 | the lamp strikes with a flicker; an amber wash spreads from the projector axis over every pre-1940 building | crane up and back (el 11 → 36, d 0.72 → 1.85) | the hole appears as the camera rises; readout 23 % |
| 4 | 6.0–11.6 | 14 May 1940 stamp in the hole (6.0), the city hall pinned (7.8) | slow push and orbit (az 128 → 104, d 1.85 → 1.62) | short suck-out before the date hit |
| 5 | 11.6–17.1 | four post-war layers switch on building by building (1.0 / 0.9 / 0.9 / 0.75 s spreads), year counter, legend rows; Kop van Zuid pinned at 14.6 | orbit to the south-east with a rise (az 104 → 52, d 1.62 → 2.75) | acceleration by spread, not by tempo |
| 6 | 18.0–21.6 | a soft level of light climbs every facade (heights ramp, 25 m rings), the reading rides up Zalmhaven I to 203 m | boom down to a low angle (el 36 → 17, d 1.95) | towers against black |
| 7 | 21.6–22.8 | projector dark | drift | silence |
| 8 | 22.8–27.0 | winter sun at the real azimuth, clock 10:55 → 12:40 (solar noon), data put away, shade projected blue | rise and turn (az 34 → 28, el 24) | first sound after the silence: brass in A♭ |
| 9 | 27.0–35.4 | the tower's noon shadow traced (fill + edge) as a range line grows 0 → 777 m with 100 m ticks; 16 roofs ping on (29.4–31.2), 9 amber | side-on from the south-east, closing in (az 40 → 32, d 1.6 → 1.16) | **signature**: poster at 30.4 s |
| 10 | 35.4–40.0 | house lights up, data off, end card | pull back and rise (d 1.3 → 2.85, el 35 → 44) | bookend |

## Score structure

100 BPM, 4/4; every layer onset, the date, the top of the climb, the sun, the line landing, the roofs and the lights sit on a beat (`demo/tools/cuecheck.py`: 0 ms on 19 cues).

| Section | Time | Palette | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| White | 0–1.8 | bowed vibraphone G4/C5, room tone, idle projector fan | |
| Lamp | 1.8–6.0 | relay, lamp strike, wash air swell; contrabass C2 + cellos G2, bowed vibraphone E♭5, a quiet marimba pulse in 8ths | suck-out 5.55–6.0 |
| Date | 6.0 | timpani C3, gran cassa, gong, bass drum, low brass stab in C minor (tuba, trombones, horns) + a 60–120 Hz punch | loudest moment of the film |
| Aftermath | 6.0–12.0 | contrabass C2, cellos E♭3, bowed vibraphone A♭4 → G4, sparse vibraphone; glass tick on the city-hall pin | |
| Growth | 12.0–18.0 | E♭ major; bass climbs E♭–F–G–A♭ one step per layer; marimba 8ths → 16ths → 16th-note triplets, pizzicato violins from layer 2, hand-chime chord per layer, horns swell from the river crossing; a soft tick per building switching on | |
| Height | 18.0–21.6 | A♭: contrabass A♭1, bowed vibraphone C5/E♭5, glockenspiel + vibraphone line climbing with the level, air riser; tubular bell E♭5 + cymbal on the top | |
| Silence | 21.6–22.8 | thin fan hum only | |
| Sun | 22.8–27.0 | horns A♭3/C4/E♭4, trombones A♭2/E♭3, tuba A♭1, timpani, gran cassa, bowed cymbal; organ (soft) and bowed vibraphone hold | second-loudest moment |
| Shadow | 27.0–31.2 | F minor floor (contrabass, cellos, soft organ), timpani heartbeat every two beats, a click per 100 m, timpani + bell when the line lands; one glass note per roof (G5 pre-war, C6 newer) | |
| Coda / lights | 31.2–40.0 | D♭ → E♭ held; at the lights a C major chord (horns, bowed vibraphone), relays, fan settling; tubular bell C5 and two glass notes on the end card | |

Mix (`demo/mix.py`): music balanced to sit 10 dB under the voice while it speaks and ducked 40 %; hits ducked 20 %, uncompressed; bus compression on music, foley and beds only; a 38 Hz high-pass (46 Hz, 4th order on hits) and a −5 dB shelf below 62 Hz on everything but the voice; master at −14.4 LUFS with a true-peak limiter at −4.6 dBTP; `mux.sh` measures the film at −13.8 LUFS, LRA 6.1 LU. `demo/tools/impactcheck.py`: the date is the loudest momentary moment, the sun −0.7 dB under it; each follows a dip of −20 and −28 dB; the silence sits 16 dB under the median program.

## Palette & props

- Model #F3F3F1 (roughness 0.88), plate water inlay (0.10, 0.13, 0.17) satin, plinth #17181A; room background a dark radial gradient.
- Layers: pre-1940 #FFA13D; 1940–64 #2A46FF; 1965–89 #2F98FF; 1990–2009 #6FDCFF; 2010–25 #E6FBFF; height ramp #1A1440 → #5A35D6 → #E2509A → #FFE7C4; projected shade #1C2C66; sun #FFD9AD; shadow trace fill (0.10, 0.22, 0.65) with a pale edge; newer shaded roofs #BFF3FF.
- Props: the model (3DBAG LOD1.3, BAG construction years), BGT water and bridge decks, the 2 m heightfield noon shadow of Zalmhaven I, the sun table for 21 Dec 2025 at 51.914° N, 4.484° E.
- Narrator: Kokoro `bm_george`, speeds 0.95–1.08.
- Real places and buildings appear as data; this is not an official film of the City of Rotterdam or of any building's owner.

## End card

Over the white model as the house lights return, a left block: 被炸平的城市怎样长回来 (Noto Sans SC 500, 64 px), *How a Flattened City Grew Back* (Inter Tight 200), an amber rule, `白模投影 · PROJECTION ON WHITE MODEL`, `3DBAG · BAG · BGT · 鹿特丹市档案馆`, `LemoLab × Claude Opus 5.5`. 35.7–40.0 s. The "LemoLab × Claude Opus 5.5" sign-off belongs to this library's demo only; a user's film carries no LemoLab credit and no copy of this card.

## Build notes

```
demo/
  build.sh       one command: data (if missing) → voice → speech check → cues → events → video → mix → master → .srt → checks → poster
  index.html     WebGL canvas + 2D overlay canvas, fonts
  main.js        render(t): camera keys, projection state per layer, overlay, window.EV, SUBCHECK
  studio.js      renderer, post, room, projection material (projLight / roofGlow), model mesh, plate, plinth, lights
  overlay.js     readouts, pins, range line, subtitle strip, end card, text registry for readcheck
  timeline.js    beats, layers, sun clock, narration (single source; tools/export.mjs → timeline.json, voice/lines.json, cues.json)
  mix.py         score, foley, beds, voice, mix → out/mix.wav + out/stems/
  tools/         prep.py (data → model, masks, stats), rd.py (RD ↔ WGS84), sun.py (solar position), fonts.py (CJK subset);
                 export.mjs (voice/cues); cuecheck.py, subcheck.mjs, motioncheck.py, impactcheck.py, finalasr.py (checks)
  data/          model.json, water.png, zshadow.png, stats.json (generated)
  assets/raw/    3DBAG and BGT downloads (gitignored)
  FACTS.md, CREDITS, TREATMENT.md, PRODUCTION_LOG.md, stills/styleframe.jpg
```

- `sh demo/build.sh` takes about 4 minutes on Apple silicon (picture ~60 s with 4 workers; TTS and the Whisper check most of the rest). `FETCH=1` re-downloads the data (~55 MB).
- Checks it runs: `asr_check.py` with `small.en` (British spellings "centre", "metres" set in the `asr` fields), cue grid, single-line subtitle widths with the real fonts (widest 618 px against 1500 px), `readcheck.mjs`, motion per second (no flat stretch; the jumps at 2.0, 2.6 and 35.6 s are the lights and the lamp), the impact ranking. `tools/finalasr.py` checks every narration line on the final mix.
- Demo-specific pitfalls: the 3DBAG WFS returns all LOD1.3 parts in one request at `count=20000` for this box (13,345 features); parts are kept only when fully inside the crop, which leaves a clean street margin at the plate edge. The heightfield shadow counts a roof as shaded when its tallest part's centroid cell is under the tower's shadow height (2 m grid); the 16 roofs are listed in `stats.json` with distances 262–734 m. Zalmhaven's 3DBAG roof (203.0 m above ground, 70th percentile of the highest part) matches the published roof height; the 12 m mast is not in the model. GTAO is faded out after the lamp strikes because it bands on the wide grazing views.

| Aftermath | 6.0–12.0 | contrabass C2, cellos E♭3, bowed vibraphone A♭4 → G4, sparse vibraphone; glass tick on the city-hall pin | |
| Growth | 12.0–18.0 | E♭ major; bass climbs E♭–F–G–A♭ one step per layer; marimba 8ths → 16ths → 16th-note triplets, pizzicato violins from layer 2, hand-chime chord per layer, horns swell from the river crossing; a soft tick per building switching on | |
| Height | 18.0–21.6 | A♭: contrabass A♭1, bowed vibraphone C5/E♭5, glockenspiel + vibraphone line climbing with the level, air riser; tubular bell E♭5 + cymbal on the top | |
| Silence | 21.6–22.8 | thin fan hum only | |
| Sun | 22.8–27.0 | horns A♭3/C4/E♭4, trombones A♭2/E♭3, tuba A♭1, timpani, gran cassa, bowed cymbal; organ (soft) and bowed vibraphone hold | second-loudest moment |
| Shadow | 27.0–31.2 | F minor floor (contrabass, cellos, soft organ), timpani heartbeat every two beats, a click per 100 m, timpani + bell when the line lands; one glass note per roof (G5 pre-war, C6 newer) | |
| Coda / lights | 31.2–40.0 | D♭ → E♭ held; at the lights a C major chord (horns, bowed vibraphone), relays, fan settling; tubular bell C5 and two glass notes on the end card | |

Mix (`demo/mix.py`): music balanced to sit 10 dB under the voice while it speaks and ducked 40 %; hits ducked 20 %, uncompressed; bus compression on music, foley and beds only; a 38 Hz high-pass (46 Hz, 4th order on hits) and a −5 dB shelf below 62 Hz on everything but the voice; master at −14.4 LUFS with a true-peak limiter at −4.6 dBTP; `mux.sh` measures the film at −13.8 LUFS, LRA 6.1 LU. `demo/tools/impactcheck.py`: the date is the loudest momentary moment, the sun −0.7 dB under it; each follows a dip of −20 and −28 dB; the silence sits 16 dB under the median program.

engine_and_build.required_engine_spec_verbatim:
- `demo/studio.js` — `makeStudio(W, H, model)`: renderer, post, room, the projection material (`projMaterial(kind)` injects `projLight()` / `roofGlow()` into MeshStandardMaterial), the city mesh (`buildCity`: outward normals, shared walls removed), plate, plinth, house light (index 0) and sun (index 1). Uniforms `U` drive every layer.
- `demo/tools/prep.py` — **3DBAG + BGT only**: it reads 3DBAG fields (`b3_h_70p`, `b3_h_maaiveld`, `oorspronkelijkbouwjaar`) and Dutch RD coordinates (`tools/rd.py`). Another source needs its own adapter that writes the same `model.json`: `{size:[w,d] model metres, b:[[year|0, height_m], …] per building, p:[[building_index, height_model_m, [[[x,z],…] outer ring, …holes]], …] per roof part, decks:[[[x,z],…]]}`, with x east, z south, 1 unit = 1 model metre; plus `water.png` (plate-sized mask) and a `stats.json` with every on-screen number. `tools/sun.py` (solar position, any place and date) and the heightfield shadow are source-independent.
- `demo/overlay.js` — readout, pin, measured range line, subtitle strip, title card; registers texts for readcheck.
- **Extra packages and packs**: none beyond `setup.sh deps` (+ `voice`, `music` for narration and score); downloads are plain `curl` from the data portal. Reprojecting another country's data may need pyproj or shapely: the agent installs them itself into a private venv in the project folder, not into `$LIB/.venv`.
- Minimal example, not in the demo: set `U.uPreC` to a station and `U.uPreR` growing to light everything within walking distance; or put a flood height in `U.uHgtF` with `U.uHgtBand` held at 1 and leave it still.

```
demo/
  build.sh       one command: data (if missing) → voice → speech check → cues → events → video → mix → master → .srt → checks → poster
  index.html     WebGL canvas + 2D overlay canvas, fonts
  main.js        render(t): camera keys, projection state per layer, overlay, window.EV, SUBCHECK
  studio.js      renderer, post, room, projection material (projLight / roofGlow), model mesh, plate, plinth, lights
  overlay.js     readouts, pins, range line, subtitle strip, end card, text registry for readcheck
  timeline.js    beats, layers, sun clock, narration (single source; tools/export.mjs → timeline.json, voice/lines.json, cues.json)
  mix.py         score, foley, beds, voice, mix → out/mix.wav + out/stems/
  tools/         prep.py (data → model, masks, stats), rd.py (RD ↔ WGS84), sun.py (solar position), fonts.py (CJK subset);
                 export.mjs (voice/cues); cuecheck.py, subcheck.mjs, motioncheck.py, impactcheck.py, finalasr.py (checks)
  data/          model.json, water.png, zshadow.png, stats.json (generated)
  assets/raw/    3DBAG and BGT downloads (gitignored)
  FACTS.md, CREDITS, TREATMENT.md, PRODUCTION_LOG.md, stills/styleframe.jpg
```

- `sh demo/build.sh` takes about 4 minutes on Apple silicon (picture ~60 s with 4 workers; TTS and the Whisper check most of the rest). `FETCH=1` re-downloads the data (~55 MB).
- Checks it runs: `asr_check.py` with `small.en` (British spellings "centre", "metres" set in the `asr` fields), cue grid, single-line subtitle widths with the real fonts (widest 618 px against 1500 px), `readcheck.mjs`, motion per second (no flat stretch; the jumps at 2.0, 2.6 and 35.6 s are the lights and the lamp), the impact ranking. `tools/finalasr.py` checks every narration line on the final mix.
- Demo-specific pitfalls: the 3DBAG WFS returns all LOD1.3 parts in one request at `count=20000` for this box (13,345 features); parts are kept only when fully inside the crop, which leaves a clean street margin at the plate edge. The heightfield shadow counts a roof as shaded when its tallest part's centroid cell is under the tower's shadow height (2 m grid); the 16 roofs are listed in `stats.json` with distances 262–734 m. Zalmhaven's 3DBAG roof (203.0 m above ground, 70th percentile of the highest part) matches the published roof height; the 12 m mast is not in the model. GTAO is faded out after the lamp strikes because it bands on the wide grazing views.

#!/bin/sh
# One command: 《被炸平的城市怎样长回来》 How a Flattened City Grew Back (Projection on White Model demo)
#   sh demo/build.sh            data (if missing) -> voice -> checks -> events -> picture -> score + mix -> master -> .srt -> checks -> poster
#   FETCH=1 sh demo/build.sh    first re-download 3DBAG LOD1.3 + BGT water and bridge decks (~55 MB into assets/raw/)
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)                 # .../<slug>/demo
FILM=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)                         # .../<slug>
LIB=${LIB:-$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)}            # films/<slug>/demo or styles/<slug>/demo -> library root
export LIB
[ -f "$LIB/core/render/video.mjs" ] || { echo "set LIB to the library folder"; exit 1; }
PY="$LIB/.venv/bin/python"
NAME=white-model
BBOX=91500,435200,94300,438000                       # RD New (EPSG:28992), wider than the model crop
cd "$LIB"

if [ "${FETCH:-0}" = "1" ] || [ ! -f "$HERE/assets/raw/l13_0.json" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$HERE/assets/raw"
  curl -sf -m 600 -o "$HERE/assets/raw/l13_0.json" "https://data.3dbag.nl/api/BAG3D/wfs?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetFeature&typeNames=BAG3D:lod13&count=20000&startIndex=0&outputFormat=application/json&bbox=$BBOX,EPSG:28992&sortBy=fid"
  for c in waterdeel overbruggingsdeel; do
    curl -sf -m 300 -o "$HERE/assets/raw/$c.json" "https://api.pdok.nl/lv/bgt/ogc/v1/collections/$c/items?bbox=$BBOX&bbox-crs=http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/28992&crs=http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/28992&limit=1000&f=json"
  done
fi
mkdir -p "$HERE/data" "$HERE/out"
"$PY" -I "$HERE/tools/prep.py" "$HERE" > "$HERE/out/prep.log"      # model.json, water.png, zshadow.png, stats.json (every number on screen)
# fonts (gitignored .woff2, subset from Google Fonts): fetch when any is missing
for f in NotoSansSC-300 NotoSansSC-500 InterTight-200 InterTight-400 IBMPlexMono-400; do
  [ -f "$HERE/fonts/$f.woff2" ] || { "$PY" -I "$HERE/tools/fonts.py" "$HERE"; break; }
done

# voice: Kokoro (bm_george), speech-to-text check with the small English model, cues from the real durations
node "$HERE/tools/export.mjs" "$HERE" > /dev/null || true
"$PY" core/tts/tts.py "$HERE/voice/lines.json" "$HERE/voice/out"
WHISPER_MODEL=small.en "$PY" core/tts/asr_check.py "$HERE/voice/lines.json" "$HERE/voice/out" --lang en
node "$HERE/tools/export.mjs" "$HERE"                # cues.json; fails on overlap

# picture, events, score + mix, master, subtitles
node core/render/events.mjs "$HERE"
node core/render/video.mjs "$HERE" --fps 24 --workers 4 --out "$HERE/out/video.mp4"
"$PY" "$HERE/mix.py"
sh core/render/mux.sh "$HERE/out/video.mp4" "$HERE/out/mix.wav" "$FILM/$NAME.mp4" 24 1
"$PY" core/render/srt.py "$HERE/out/cues_srt.json" "$FILM/$NAME.srt"

# checks
"$PY" -I "$HERE/tools/cuecheck.py" "$HERE" | tail -1
node "$HERE/tools/subcheck.mjs" "$HERE" | tail -1
node core/render/readcheck.mjs "$HERE" > "$HERE/out/readcheck.txt" && echo "readcheck ok"
"$PY" -I "$HERE/tools/motioncheck.py" "$FILM/$NAME.mp4" | tail -2
"$PY" -I "$HERE/tools/impactcheck.py" "$HERE" | tail -4

# poster (the signature shot) and the gallery style frame
mkdir -p "$HERE/stills"
ffmpeg -v error -y -ss 30.4 -i "$FILM/$NAME.mp4" -frames:v 1 -q:v 2 "$FILM/poster.jpg"
cp "$FILM/poster.jpg" "$HERE/stills/styleframe.jpg"
echo "done: $FILM/$NAME.mp4"

usage: python -I tools/prep.py <demo_dir>

Every number the film shows is computed here and written to data/stats.json (the page only reads it)."""

inside = lambda ring: all(X0 <= x <= X1 and Y0 <= y <= Y1 for x, y, *_ in ring)
def area(r): return abs(sum(r[i][0] * r[i + 1][1] - r[i + 1][0] * r[i][1] for i in range(len(r) - 1)) / 2)
def ring_c(r): n = len(r) - 1; return (sum(q[0] for q in r[:-1]) / n, sum(q[1] for q in r[:-1]) / n)
loc = lambda x, y: [round((x - CX) * S, 5), round(-(y - CY) * S, 5)]

B, parts, skipped = {}, [], 0
for f in feats:
    p, g = f['properties'], f['geometry']
    if p.get('b3_h_70p') is None or p.get('b3_h_maaiveld') is None: skipped += 1; continue
    h = p['b3_h_70p'] - p['b3_h_maaiveld']
    if h < 1.5 or h > 260: skipped += 1; continue
    for poly in ([g['coordinates']] if g['type'] == 'Polygon' else g['coordinates']):
        if not inside(poly[0]): continue
        bid = p['identificatie']
        b = B.setdefault(bid, {'id': bid, 'year': p.get('oorspronkelijkbouwjaar') or 0, 'h': 0, 'a': 0, 'polys': []})
        if h > b['h']: b['top'] = ring_c(poly[0])
        b['h'] = max(b['h'], h); b['a'] += area(poly[0]); b['polys'].append((h, poly))
        parts.append((bid, h, poly))

blist = sorted(B.values(), key=lambda b: b['id'])
idx = {b['id']: i for i, b in enumerate(blist)}

# bridge decks (BGT overbruggingsdeel), clipped to the crop: low white slabs across the water
def clip(poly):
    def cl(pts, inside_, inter):
        out = []
        for i in range(len(pts)):
            a, b = pts[i - 1], pts[i]
            if inside_(b):
                if not inside_(a): out.append(inter(a, b))
                out.append(b)
            elif inside_(a): out.append(inter(a, b))
        return out
    pts = [tuple(q[:2]) for q in poly[:-1]]
    for axis, lim, keep_ge in ((0, X0, True), (0, X1, False), (1, Y0, True), (1, Y1, False)):
        if not pts: break
        ins = (lambda q, a=axis, l=lim, g=keep_ge: q[a] >= l if g else q[a] <= l)
        def inter(a, b, ax=axis, l=lim):
            t = (l - a[ax]) / (b[ax] - a[ax]); return (a[0] + t * (b[0] - a[0]), a[1] + t * (b[1] - a[1]))
        pts = cl(pts, ins, inter)
    return pts
decks = []
for f in json.load(open(os.path.join(R, 'overbruggingsdeel.json')))['features']:
    if f['properties'].get('eind_registratie') is not None: continue
    g = f['geometry']
    for poly in ([g['coordinates']] if g['type'] == 'Polygon' else g['coordinates']):
        c = clip(poly[0])
        if len(c) >= 3 and area(c + [c[0]]) > 20: decks.append([loc(x, y) for x, y in c])

out = {'scale': S, 'crop': [X0, X1, Y0, Y1], 'size': [(X1 - X0) * S, (Y1 - Y0) * S], 'bands': BANDS,
       'b': [[b['year'], round(b['h'], 1)] for b in blist],
       'p': [[idx[bid], round(h * S, 5), [[loc(x, y) for x, y, *_ in r[:-1]] for r in poly]] for bid, h, poly in parts],
       'decks': decks}
json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(D, 'data/model.json'), 'w'), separators=(',', ':'))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ water mask (BGT waterdeel, current records)
MW = 4096; MH = round(MW * (Y1 - Y0) / (X1 - X0))
im = Image.new('L', (MW, MH), 0); d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
P = lambda r: [((x - X0) / (X1 - X0) * MW, (Y1 - y) / (Y1 - Y0) * MH) for x, y, *_ in r]
for w in json.load(open(os.path.join(R, 'waterdeel.json')))['features']:
    if w['properties']['eind_registratie'] is not None: continue
    g = w['geometry']
    for poly in ([g['coordinates']] if g['type'] == 'Polygon' else g['coordinates']):
        d.polygon(P(poly[0]), fill=255)
        for hole in poly[1:]: d.polygon(P(hole), fill=0)
im.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(1.2)).save(os.path.join(D, 'data/water.png'))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ stats
def pos(b): return loc(*b['top']) + [round(b['h'] * S, 5)]
yrs = [b for b in blist if b['year'] > 1200]
tot_a = sum(b['a'] for b in yrs)
bands = []
for lo, hi in BANDS:
    m = [b for b in yrs if lo <= b['year'] < hi]
    bands.append({'lo': lo, 'hi': hi, 'n': len(m), 'area_share': round(sum(b['a'] for b in m) / tot_a, 4),
                  'mean_h': round(sum(b['h'] for b in m) / max(len(m), 1), 1), 'over100': sum(1 for b in m if b['h'] > 100)})
tall = sorted(blist, key=lambda b: -b['h'])
def near_rd(x, y, r=60):
    c = [b for b in blist if (b['top'][0] - x) ** 2 + (b['top'][1] - y) ** 2 < r * r]
    return max(c, key=lambda b: b['a']) if c else None
marks = {}
for name, (x, y) in {'laurens': (92970, 437394), 'stadhuis': to_rd(4.4796, 51.9227), 'zalmhaven': tall[0]['top']}.items():   # Zalmhaven I = the tallest roof (NL.IMBAG.Pand.0599100100020122)
    b = tall[0] if name == 'zalmhaven' else near_rd(x, y); marks[name] = {'id': b['id'], 'year': b['year'], 'h': round(b['h'], 1), 'pos': pos(b), 'bi': idx[b['id']]}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ winter-solstice noon shadow on a 2 m height grid
lon_c, lat_c = to_wgs(CX, CY)
sun = []
for m in range(8 * 60 + 30, 16 * 60 + 31, 5):
    alt, az = solar(2025, 12, 21, (m - 60) / 60, lat_c, lon_c); sun.append([m, round(alt, 3), round(az, 3)])
noon = max(sun, key=lambda s: s[1])
G = 2.0; GW, GH = int((X1 - X0) / G), int((Y1 - Y0) / G)
def hmap(polys):
    img = Image.new('F', (GW, GH), 0.); dr = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    for h, poly in sorted(polys, key=lambda q: q[0]):
        dr.polygon([((x - X0) / G, (Y1 - y) / G) for x, y, *_ in poly[0]], fill=float(h))
    return np.array(img)
Hall = hmap([(h, poly) for _, h, poly in parts])
zb = B[marks['zalmhaven']['id']]
Hz = hmap(zb['polys'])
alt, az = math.radians(noon[1]), math.radians(noon[2])
dx, dy = math.sin(az), -math.cos(az)          # toward the sun in grid (col, row): east = +col, north = -row
def shadow_by(src, maxlen=1200):
    sh = np.zeros_like(Hall, bool); tan = math.tan(alt)
    for k in range(1, int(maxlen / G)):
        ox, oy = int(round(k * dx)), int(round(k * dy))
        s = np.zeros_like(src)
        ys0, ys1 = max(0, -oy), min(GH, GH - oy); xs0, xs1 = max(0, -ox), min(GW, GW - ox)
        s[ys0:ys1, xs0:xs1] = src[ys0 + oy:ys1 + oy, xs0 + ox:xs1 + ox]
        sh |= s - k * G * tan > Hall + .5
    return sh
Sz = shadow_by(Hz)
Image.fromarray(((Sz & ~(Hz > 0)) * 255).astype(np.uint8)).filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(1.5)).save(os.path.join(D, 'data/zshadow.png'))   # the tower's noon shadow, 2 m grid
mine = Hz > 0
shaded = []
for b in blist:
    if b['id'] == zb['id']: continue
    cx, cy = b['top']; c, r = int((cx - X0) / G), int((Y1 - cy) / G)
    if 0 <= r < GH and 0 <= c < GW and Sz[r, c] and not mine[r, c]: shaded.append(b)
ys, xs = np.nonzero(Sz & ~mine)
reach = float(np.max(np.hypot((xs * G + X0) - zb['top'][0], (Y1 - ys * G) - zb['top'][1]))) if len(xs) else 0
stats = {
    'buildings': len(blist), 'parts': len(parts), 'decks': len(decks), 'skipped_parts': skipped, 'year_unknown': len(blist) - len(yrs),
    'bands': bands, 'pre1940_area_share': bands[0]['area_share'],
    'over100': sum(1 for b in blist if b['h'] > 100),
    'tallest': [{'id': b['id'], 'h': round(b['h'], 1), 'year': b['year'], 'pos': pos(b)} for b in tall[:8]],
    'marks': marks, 'centre_wgs': [round(lon_c, 5), round(lat_c, 5)],
    'sun': sun, 'sun_noon': {'min': noon[0], 'alt': noon[1], 'az': noon[2]},
    'zalm_shadow': {'theory_m': round(zb['h'] / math.tan(alt), 1), 'reach_m': round(reach, 1), 'shaded_roofs': len(shaded),
                    'shaded_pre1940': sum(1 for b in shaded if 0 < b['year'] < 1940),
                    'shaded': sorted([{'bi': idx[b['id']], 'year': b['year'], 'h': round(b['h'], 1), 'pos': pos(b),
                                       'd': round(math.hypot(b['top'][0] - zb['top'][0], b['top'][1] - zb['top'][1]), 1)} for b in shaded], key=lambda q: q['d'])},
}
json.dump(stats, open(os.path.join(D, 'data/stats.json'), 'w'), indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in stats.items() if k not in ('sun', 'tallest', 'zalm_shadow')} | {'tallest': [(t['h'], t['year']) for t in stats['tallest']]}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=0)[:3000])

# 事实表：《被炸平的城市怎样长回来》

片中每一个数字、年份和事实性说法都在下表里：说法 → 出处（URL）→ 原文引用。核对日期：2026-10-16。

两类数字要分开看：

- **官方 / 公开来源的说法**（下表 A）：鹿特丹市档案馆（Stadsarchief Rotterdam，市政府机构）的原文；Zalmhaven 的屋面高度另以维基百科条目为参照，并与本片的实测值互相印证。
- **数据实测**（下表 B）：本片用公开数据自己算的（建成年代占比、各年代栋数、百米高楼数、屋面高度、太阳高度、影长、影中屋顶数）。算法全部在 `tools/prep.py`，结果写在 `data/stats.json`，页面只读这个文件。画面上标了"按建筑占地面积 · BAG 建成年份""3DBAG 激光实测""太阳位置按天文算法"。

## A. 史实与公开来源

| # | 片中说法（画面 / 旁白） | 出处 | 原文 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | 钉标"1940.5.14  13:27"；旁白 "May fourteenth, nineteen forty."；字幕"1940 年 5 月 14 日。" | 鹿特丹市档案馆《Rotterdam in oorlog》 https://stadsarchief.rotterdam.nl/rotterdam-oorlog | "Daarom bombarderen Duitse Heinkels op 14 mei 1940 om 13.27 uur de binnenstad van Rotterdam." |
| A2 | 旁白 "Bombs and fire took much of the centre."；字幕"炸弹和大火吞掉了大片市中心。" | 同 A1 | "Binnen een kwartier zijn grote delen van de binnenstad verwoest." / "De bommen en de branden daarna verwoesten 25.000 woningen en 11.000 andere panden." |
| A3 | 钉标副行"258 公顷城区成为废墟" | 同 A1 | "Een oppervlakte van 258 hectare stad ligt in puin." |
| A4 | 钉标"市政厅 · 1920 / 轰炸中几乎完好" | 鹿特丹市档案馆《Het stadhuis tijdens het bombardement》 https://stadsarchief.rotterdam.nl/het-stadhuis-tijdens-het-bombardement ；年份 1920 见 B3 | "Maar hoe kan het dat zo'n groot gebouw de verwoesting van 14 mei 1940 vrijwel ongeschonden heeft doorstaan?" / "Het vuur krijgt geen vat op het vrijstaande stadhuis." |
| A5 | 钉标"Kop van Zuid / 马斯河南岸"（钉在 Wilhelminapier） | Wikipedia《Kop van Zuid》 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kop_van_Zuid | "…located on the south bank of the Nieuwe Maas opposite the center of town." / 该区 "includes the Wilhelmina Pier" |
| A6 | 钉标"Zalmhaven I / 屋面 203 m"（口径：屋面，不含桅杆） | Wikipedia《De Zalmhaven》 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Zalmhaven ；与 B5 的实测值一致 | "The main tower of the complex, Zalmhaven I, reaches 215 metres (705 ft) in height," / "The roof height is 203 metres (666 ft), while the mast takes up the last 12 metres (39 ft) of height." |
| A7 | 钉标"Zalmhaven I / 2022 年建成" | BAG 原始建成年份 2022（B5）；Wikipedia 同上 | "…the entire project was completed in April 2022." |

说明：样片里曾用"圣劳伦斯教堂 · 15 世纪"作标签，但 BAG 登记的原始建成年份是 1640（塔楼加高年代），教堂官网只写 "The Laurenskerk is the only remaining late Gothic building from the medieval Rotterdam."（https://laurenskerk.nl/en/visit/），没有给出建造年份；为免两种口径打架，正式片不再给教堂标年份，改用市档案馆有原文的市政厅。

## B. 数据实测（本片自己算的）

数据：3DBAG（LOD1.3 屋面分块，AHN 激光点云重建，CC BY 4.0）+ 其中带的 BAG 字段 `oorspronkelijkbouwjaar`（原始建成年份，CC0）；BGT 水面与桥面（CC0）。模型范围：RD 坐标 x 91700–94000、y 435300–437900（2.3 × 2.6 km，中心 51.914°N、4.484°E）。只保留完全落在范围内的屋面分块：3,887 栋楼、8,860 个分块。楼高 = 该分块屋面 70 分位高度 − 地面高度（`b3_h_70p − b3_h_maaiveld`），一栋楼取最高分块。

| B2 | 年代图例"1940–1964 · 1,113 栋 / 1965–1989 · 522 栋 / 1990–2009 · 413 栋 / 2010–2025 · 233 栋"；滚动年份 1940 → 2025 | 按原始建成年份分档计数 | 1,113 / 522 / 413 / 233 |
| B3 | 市政厅"1920" | BAG 原始建成年份（NL.IMBAG.Pand.0599100000701897） | 1920 |
| B4 | 读数"24/25 · 百米高楼，1990 后建"；旁白 "Twenty-four of its twenty-five tallest…"（字幕："最高的 25 栋里，24 栋建于 1990 年后"） | 楼高 > 100 m 的楼按年代分档 | 共 25 栋：1965–89 有 1 栋，1990–2009 有 13 栋，2010–25 有 11 栋 → 24/25。高于 100 m 的正好是最高的 25 栋 |
| B5 | "Zalmhaven I · 屋面 203 m · 2022 年建成"；高度图例上限 203 m；"最高那栋楼" | NL.IMBAG.Pand.0599100100020122，模型中屋面最高的楼 | 203.0 m，BAG 年份 2022 |
| B6 | "14.6° · 冬至正午太阳高度"；旁白 "below fifteen degrees"；时钟落在 12:40 | NOAA/Meeus 太阳位置算法（`tools/sun.py`），2025-12-21，CET（UTC+1），模型中心经纬度；逐 5 分钟取高度最大值 | 12:40 CET，高度 14.647°，方位 179.94° |
| B7 | "777 m · 冬至正午的影长"；旁白 "nearly eight hundred metres" | 影长 = 屋面高度 ÷ tan(太阳高度) = 203.0 ÷ tan 14.647°；另在 2 m 网格上做高度场光线步进，影子实际末端距塔顶分块中心 784 m | 776.6 m → 777 m |
| B8 | "16 个屋顶落在它的影里 · 其中 9 栋建于 1940 年以前"；旁白 "across sixteen roofs. Nine were there before the war." | 2 m 网格高度场：对每个格子沿太阳方向步进，若 Zalmhaven I 的高度减去 距离 × tan(高度角) 仍高于该格屋面 0.5 m 以上，则该格在它的影中；一栋楼的最高分块中心格在影中即计入 | 16 栋（距塔 262–734 m），其中 BAG 年份 < 1940 的 9 栋（1928–1939） |

"战前就在"（Nine were there before the war）指 BAG 原始建成年份早于 1940、今天仍在的楼。
